declarations.name: InstrumentActivityResult
declarations.comment:
A structure containing the activity levels and detected time ranges for instruments in a song.

The ``activity`` property provides a continuous signal for each instrument. The values range from `0.0`, not present to `1.0`, fully active. The ``ranges`` property
provides discrete time windows during which the framework detected each instrument.
Use both properties together to determine when an instrument is present and how prominently it features at each moment.

members.name: ranges
members.comment: The time ranges during which each instrument is detected.

members.name: activity
members.comment: The activity level of each instrument over time, as values from 0.0 to 1.0.

declarations.name: KeyResult
declarations.comment:
A value describing the musical key detected over a time range.

A key is the central note that organizes a piece of music. The tonic can be any of the supported enharmonic spellings: A, A♭, A♯, B♭, B, C, C♯, D♭, D, D♯, E♭, E, F, F♯, G, G♭, G♯. Enharmonic equivalents are represented as distinct cases to preserve the original spelling.
A musical key defined by a tonic note and a mode.

members.name: ranges
members.comment: The detected key for each time range.

declarations.comment:

A key signature pairs a root note, ``tonic`` with a ``mode``, major or minor to describe the harmonic center of a section of audio.

members.comment: The mode of the musical key.

members.comment: The root note of the musical key.

declarations.name: LoudnessResult
declarations.comment:
A structure that contains perceptual loudness measurements for a song, including integrated, momentary, short-term, and peak values.
## Discussion
The `LoudnessResult` delivers perceptual loudness measurements that align with human hearing perception, using the Loudness K-weighted Full Scale (LUFS) standard defined in ITU-R BS.1770.

The results contain time-based measurements including integrated loudness, short-term loudness, momentary loudness, and peak amplitude.

When used in `SessionResult`, a single `LoudnessResult` contains all analysis values for the entire song, with `momentary` and `shortTerm` arrays containing the complete set of measurements across the song's duration.

When used in the streaming `loudnessResults` context, the framework delivers multiple results progressively during analysis. Each result's ``LoudnessResult/momentary`` and ``LoudnessResult/shortTerm`` arrays contain only one value representing the measurement at that point in time.

members.name: integrated
members.comment: The integrated loudness of the song, measured in LUFS over its full duration.

members.name: peak
members.comment: The peak amplitude of the song in decibels (dB).

members.name: momentary
members.comment:
An array of momentary loudness measurements sampled across the song in LUFS.

The measurement happens in 400 millisecond (ms) increments that advance 100ms at a time.

members.name: shortTerm
members.comment:
An array of short-term loudness measurements sampled across the song in LUFS.

Short-term loudness is a 3 second window that advances 100 milliseconds (ms) per result.

members.name: unownedExecutor
members.signature: nonisolated final var unownedExecutor: UnownedSerialExecutor { get }
members.comment:
Retrieve the executor for this actor as an optimized, unowned
reference.

This property must always evaluate to the same executor for a
given actor instance, and holding on to the actor must keep the
executor alive.

This property will be implicitly accessed when work needs to be
scheduled onto this actor.  These accesses may be merged,
eliminated, and rearranged with other work, and they may even
be introduced when not strictly required.  Visible side effects
are therefore strongly discouraged within this property.

- SeeAlso: ``SerialExecutor``
- SeeAlso: ``TaskExecutor``

members.name: init
members.signature: convenience init(asset: any AVAsset & Sendable) async throws
members.comment:
Creates a music understanding session from an audio asset.

Use this initializer when your audio source is an AVAsset rather than a streaming sequence of audio buffers.

- Parameter asset: An `AVAsset` containing an audio track.

- Throws: If the asset is unreadable, does not contain valid audio tracks, has protected content, or cannot be processed for analysis.

- Note: This initializer does not support HTTP live streams (HLS). The asset must represent locally available media or a complete file.

members.name: cancel
members.comment:
Cancels any ongoing analysis.

Once a session has been canceled it cannot be re-used.

members.name: analyze
members.signature: @discardableResult func analyze(for analysisTypes: Set<AnalysisType>) async throws -> MusicUnderstandingSession.SessionResult
members.comment:
Performs the specified analyses on the session's audio source.

- Parameter analysisTypes: A `Set` of `AnalysisType` values specifying which analyses to perform.

- Returns: The aggregated session result containing all requested analyses.

- Throws: If the analysis types set is empty, or if analysis is already running on this session.

- Note: Call this method only once per session instance. Create a new session to run additional analyses.

Example usage:
   ```swift
   let session = MusicUnderstandingSession(audioProvider: provider)
   let result = try await session.analyze(for: [.rhythm, .pace, .loudness])
   ```

members.name: analyze
members.comment:
Performs all available analyses on the session's audio source.

- Returns: The aggregated session result containing all analyses.

- Throws: If analysis is already running on this session.

- Note: This method can only be called once per session instance. Create a new session to run additional analyses.

Example usage:
```swift
let session = MusicUnderstandingSession(audioProvider: provider)
let result = try await session.analyze()
```

declarations.name: StructureResult
declarations.comment:
A structure that provides a song's structure boundary information including sections, segments, and phrases.

The `StructureResult` describes a song's structure in terms of sections, segments and phrases.
A section corresponds to a distinct part of a song, such as an intro, verse, or chorus.
A section consists of one or more segments, and each segment consists of one or more phrases.

members.name: phrases
members.comment:
The time range of each phrase in the song.

A phrase is a group of bars that form a distinct part of a song.

members.name: sections
members.comment:
The time ranges of each section in the song.

A section contains one or more segments and represents a major structural component, such as a verse or chorus.

members.name: segments
members.comment:
The time range of each segment in the song.

A segment is a collection of phrases that form a distinct part of a song.
